record.original_question: Does there exist an infinite square-free word w and an infinite conducting sequence beta such that w is the shuffle of w with itself determined by beta?

evidence.quote: Is there an infinite square-free word w such that w = w  beta w for some infinitebeta?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let A be a finite alphabet and let A^ω denote the set of infinite words over A. A finite or infinite word is square-free if it contains no nonempty factor of the form xx. Given two infinite words u = u_1 u_2 u_3 … and v = v_1 v_2 v_3 … over A and an infinite binary sequence β = b_1 b_2 b_3 … ∈ {u,v}^ω in which both letters u and v occur infinitely often, the shuffle of u and v directed by β is the infinite word obtained by reading, for k = 1, 2, 3, …, the next unused letter of u when b_k = u and the next unused letter of v when b_k = v. 

An infinite word w ∈ A^ω is said to be self-shuffling if there exists an infinite directing sequence β such that the shuffle of w with itself directed by β equals w itself.

Question: Does there exist an infinite square-free word w (over some finite alphabet) that is self-shuffling, i.e. such that w equals the shuffle of w with itself determined by some infinite directing sequence β?
artifact.status_search_result: The question (posed by Harju) was answered affirmatively by Müller, Puzynina, and Rao in "Infinite square-free self-shuffling words" (arXiv:1401.6536), which constructs infinite square-free words that are self-shuffling.

status_evidence.title: Infinite square-free self-shuffling words
status_evidence.snippet: We answer this question affirmatively regarding whether square-free self-shuffling words exist.
status_evidence.claim: Existence of infinite square-free self-shuffling words is proved.

status_evidence.title: On Shuffling of Infinite Square-Free Words
status_evidence.snippet: Paper on shuffling of infinite square-free words in Electronic Journal of Combinatorics.
status_evidence.claim: Related published result confirming the affirmative answer.
